title: Bind research source reads to original Git objects
body:
## Summary

Local Git replacement refs can make the source readers return an original blob ID with a replacement's bytes. Scaffolding can then accept altered working bytes and record pins that fail in a clean checkout; an export can likewise contain replacement bytes under the original publication commit.

Set `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` only for the shared Git readers' subprocesses. Single reads, HEAD inventories, both batch protocols, scaffolding, metadata validation, publication-byte comparison and exports now read the stored objects. Six synthetic Git regressions cover blob and commit replacements, custom replacement namespaces, newline-path fallback, forged live pins, and actual exported bytes/receipts. The parent environment and replacement refs are unchanged.

This is a `portable-replay` source/byte-binding repair, separate from the optional ancestry check. It does not establish source availability, mathematical correctness, or a new selected result. Credit Nick Petalas's [PR3304](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3304) for the preceding immutable-object ancestry policy, Douglas Colkitt for the shared runner/scaffold, and Tekalign for the exporter.

Base: canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6, refetched unchanged. Overlap checked 325 open PRs, 2,959 closed PRs and 2,444 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings; PR3304 explicitly left the shared readers unchanged. This is not an exhaustive novelty claim.

## Test plan

- [x] All six new regression methods fail against the unmodified base reader: five assertion failures and one byte-mismatch error.
- [x] 67 focused tests pass on macOS with CPython 3.12.14 and Git 2.54.0, including existing batch compatibility, path spelling, scaffold, publication-byte, source-history and exporter controls.
- [x] All six new regressions also pass under optimized Python with warnings treated as errors.
- [x] `git diff --check` passes.
- [ ] Hosted CI on this PR; no historical mathematical replay or selected-frontier cold replay is claimed.

Run from the repository root with Python 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -W error -B - <<'PY'
import sys
import unittest

patterns = [
    'test_research_git_*.py',
    'test_research_scaffold_batch.py',
    'test_research_commit_bytes.py',
    'test_research_source_history.py',
    'test_research_export.py',
]
suite = unittest.TestSuite(
    unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover('tests', pattern=pattern)
    for pattern in patterns
)
result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=1).run(suite)
sys.exit(not result.wasSuccessful())
PY
python3.12 -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_git_replacements.py' -v
git diff --check
```

Prepared for roger-sato with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in diagnosis, implementation, regression tests and writing. Apache-2.0. Same-session agent review is not independent human acceptance.
